text.arabic_uthmani: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ أَمْثَٰلَكُمْ وَنُنشِئَكُمْ فِى مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

words.gloss_range: prepositional capacity frame governing the following subjunctive clause; spatial elevation remains as image, not as local location

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the opening of the governed subjunctive complement naming what capacity covers

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) opens 56:61 as a governed capacity frame rather than an independent new sentence. It reaches back to the negated unsurpassability claim in 56:60 and forward into {{ar:أَنْ نُبَدِّلَ}} ({{tr:an nubaddila}}), so the verse boundary itself becomes part of the syntax. The spatial over/upon image survives as mastery over the act, while local grammar keeps the force in the domain of ability, not literal location. Its long opening vowel delays the first verb and then tightens toward the nasalized subjunctive onset, making the movement from decreed death in 56:60 into possible transformation in 56:61 audible as well as syntactic.

topics.headline: opening preposition specifies the prior capacity claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 56:61 begins mid-construction, specifying the domain in which the prior claim cannot be outstripped.
topics.reason: The local attachment strongly licenses the following subjunctive clause as governed by the preposition; the competing backward attachment is retained only as a reason to state the cross-ayah dependency carefully.

topics.headline: vertical mastery colors the capacity reading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the capacity claim is not flat ability language; it carries an image of mastery over the replacement act.
topics.reason: The preposition's range allows over/upon imagery while the governed clause selects a figurative capacity use.

topics.headline: opening length delays the first action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the capacity frame before the replacement verb arrives, so the act is introduced as governed power rather than bare event.
topics.reason: The ayah opens with a lengthened prepositional form before moving into the nasalized subjunctive onset.

topics.headline: death closure turns into transformation capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the move from the closed mortality claim of 56:60 to an open transformation claim in 56:61.
topics.reason: The preposition depends on the preceding discourse frame and introduces the clause that names prospective replacement and re-origination.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the preposition that governs the clause introduced here

words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the replacement action into the complement of {{ar:عَلَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), so the ayah names what divine capacity covers. Its governance begins with {{ar:نُبَدِّلَ}} ({{tr:nubaddila}}) and extends by coordination to {{ar:نُنْشِئَكُمْ}} ({{tr:nunshiʾakum}}), making the two actions one dependent capacity package. The particle is therefore best read through its maṣdar-making force here, while purpose nuance stays secondary. Because it appears immediately after the cross-boundary governor, it keeps 56:61 attached to 56:60 instead of launching a detached prediction.

topics.headline: one particle governs both actions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that replacement and re-origination are grammatically bundled as one capacity complement.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence has the particle governing the first subjunctive, with the second verb coordinated into the same construction.

topics.headline: the action is packaged as capacity content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause is not merely giving a purpose; it is naming the act over which capacity is asserted.
topics.reason: The prepositional frame selects the particle's verbal-noun-like complement effect; purpose remains a possible general value but does not control this local syntax.

topics.headline: dependency stays visible after the ayah break
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 56:61 front-loads a dependent clause, keeping the new ayah syntactically tied to the previous one.
topics.reason: The particle follows the opening preposition before any independent finite main verb appears in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: Form II subjunctive replacement directed at the following likeness-object; locally transformative substitution after the death boundary, not casual exchange
words.root_gloss_range: substitution, exchange, alteration, replacement, and substitute-giving; local Form II plus object and context select intensive transformative replacement

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the direct object, the addressees' likenesses or equivalents
the coordinated second verb in the capacity sequence

words.prose: {{ar:نُبَدِّلَ}} ({{tr:nubaddila}}) is the first action named inside the capacity clause. Its prefixed first-person plural agency is present in the verb, but the direct object is {{ar:أَمْثَالَكُمْ}} ({{tr:amthālakum}}), so the first pressure falls on the addressees' likenesses or equivalents rather than directly on the addressees themselves. The Form II shape and doubled middle consonant make the replacement thorough and transformative, while the death boundary in 56:60 narrows the root away from voluntary exchange. The root field also lets process and produced substitute converge, and the replacement-of-likeness pattern resonates with 76:28 while the final non-knowledge clause keeps the transformed equivalents beyond the addressees' grasp. The word also waits structurally for {{ar:نُنْشِئَكُمْ}} ({{tr:nunshiʾakum}}), so replacement opens a two-act capacity sequence that moves from altered likeness-patterns toward re-origination.

topics.headline: divine action remains inside the capacity frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine We is encoded in the verb, but the action is still grammatically dependent on the capacity construction.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as first-person plural imperfect subjunctive, and the particle attachment explains its dependent mood.

topics.headline: replacement targets likenesses first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first verb does not simply say the addressees are replaced; it targets their likeness-patterns as the object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the following plural possessed noun as the direct object of the replacement verb.

topics.headline: Form II makes substitution intensive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices replacement as a deep alteration after death, not a casual swap or voluntary exchange.
topics.reason: The root range is broader than the local sense, but Form II, the death context, and the object together select transformative replacement.

topics.headline: act and substitute converge in the root field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same root field can evoke both the replacing process and the resulting substitute.
topics.reason: The dictionary evidence supports related process and substitute senses, while the local verb chooses the process side.

topics.headline: replacement belongs to wider likeness and knowledge patterns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this local replacement of likenesses resonates with other replacement-and-likeness language (76:28) and is framed by final non-knowledge.
topics.reason: The echoes support a pattern and boundary, but they do not override the local object and governed subjunctive frame.

topics.headline: replacement waits for re-origination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first verb as the opening member of a paired capacity sequence rather than the whole claim.
topics.reason: The following conjunction coordinates a second subjunctive verb with this one, and the doubled consonant makes the first action's intensity audible.

words.gloss_range: your likenesses, equivalents, or patterned counterparts as the direct object of replacement; not the bare addressees themselves
words.root_gloss_range: likeness, equivalent, pattern, parable, representation; local object role selects likeness-equivalent while leaving pattern and representability nearby

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the governing replacement verb

words.prose: {{ar:أَمْثَالَكُمْ}} ({{tr:amthālakum}}) is the direct object of {{ar:نُبَدِّلَ}} ({{tr:nubaddila}}), so the ayah first names your likenesses, equivalents, or patterned counterparts as replaceable. The possessive suffix makes those equivalents specifically yours, and the plural form widens the target beyond one body into repeatable patterns. The root's parable and representation range remains nearby, but local grammar selects likeness-equivalent rather than an independent parable reading; the same-surah return from 56:23 shifts from pearl simile to the addressees' replaceable likenesses. Its final suffix then sounds forward into {{ar:نُنْشِئَكُمْ}} ({{tr:nunshiʾakum}}), carrying the addressed group from replaceable likeness-patterns into direct re-origination and toward the final clause that withholds the new mode from human knowledge.

topics.headline: the replaceable object is your likenesses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first replacement target is relationally tied to the addressees but is not simply the bare word you.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as the direct object of the replacement verb and the suffix as possessive.

topics.headline: plural likeness keeps pattern pressure alive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices replacement aimed at reproducible likeness-patterns, while the local syntax keeps equivalents as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The root family supports likeness, pattern, and parable values, but the accusative object role under the replacement verb narrows the local meaning to equivalents or likeness-patterns.

topics.headline: possession is fused into the object noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the addressed group built into the noun being replaced, not left as a separate detachable pronoun.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix binds the plural noun to the direct addressees and continues the same addressed group from 56:60.

topics.headline: likeness is sharpened by replacement governance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the representable and parabolic background of the root, while the local replacement construction makes likeness the active value.
topics.reason: The root range includes parable and representation, but immediate governance by the replacement verb narrows the local object away from ordinary parable usage.

topics.headline: the suffix carries the audience into the next act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same addressed ending moving from replaceable likenesses to the later direct object of re-origination.
topics.reason: The word precedes the second verb and shares the addressed suffix sound with it; the same word also recalls a surah-local likeness use at 56:23 with a changed function.

topics.headline: replaceable likenesses face an unknown domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the named likenesses stand before a final clause that withholds the new mode from human knowledge.
topics.reason: Co-occurrence and closure evidence support a relation between likeness and knowability, but the local noun remains governed by the replacement verb.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking the second subjunctive verb to the first under the same capacity frame

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the first coordinated subjunctive action
the second coordinated subjunctive action

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge that keeps {{ar:نُنْشِئَكُمْ}} ({{tr:nunshiʾakum}}) inside the same governed capacity construction as {{ar:نُبَدِّلَ}} ({{tr:nubaddila}}). It joins the two acts without itself deciding whether they are sequential stages or paired aspects. Because the particle is proclitic on the second verb, the re-origination beat arrives as continuation rather than restart. It also pivots the line from the named, possessed likeness-object to the unknown domain that follows.

topics.headline: the second verb stays inside the same frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that re-origination is not a detached new assertion but a coordinated part of the same capacity claim.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second verb as conjoined with the first under the particle-governed construction.

topics.headline: coordination leaves sequence open while pivoting meaning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the conjunction moving from known likeness-equivalents toward unknown mode without forcing a rigid temporal connector.
topics.reason: The conjunction links the two verbs and permits coordinated capacities without requiring a specific then/while relation.

topics.headline: short connector joins directly to the second verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second act as immediately attached to the first rather than separated by a lexical pause.
topics.reason: The conjunction is proclitic to the second verb in the surface form.

words.gloss_range: Form IV subjunctive causative re-origination with the addressees as attached direct object
words.root_gloss_range: arising, growing, producing, originating, genesis; local Form IV and divine subject select caused origination into an unknown mode

supporting_anchors.display: {{ar:فِي مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:fī mā lā taʿlamūna}})
supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the unknown domain or mode attached to re-origination

words.prose: {{ar:نُنْشِئَكُمْ}} ({{tr:nunshiʾakum}}) brings the second act into the same capacity frame, but now the attached object is the addressees themselves. The word encloses the origination root between first-person plural agency and second-person plural object, making re-origination a direct divine-to-you action. Form IV selects caused origination rather than self-emergent growth, and the root field gives the act genesis pressure. At the same time, the imperfect subjunctive keeps it projected within capacity, while the following {{ar:فِي مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:fī mā lā taʿlamūna}}) places that re-origination in an unknown mode. The hamza gives the second act a caught articulation at the break into new bringing-into-being. The word also bridges to the next ayah, where origination becomes remembered first origination (56:62), and it sits within a Surah 56 origination thread running through 56:35, 56:61, 56:62, and 56:72.

topics.headline: the addressees become the object of re-origination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from replacing your likenesses to originating you directly.
topics.reason: The second verb is coordinated under the same governed clause and carries an attached second-person plural object suffix.

topics.headline: agency and object are compressed into one verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a single word carrying both divine agency and the addressed recipients of the act.
topics.reason: The verb has first-person plural subject agreement and an attached second-person plural object pronoun.

topics.headline: Form IV selects caused origination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the act as divinely caused coming-into-being, while broader arising and growth senses are held in the background.
topics.reason: The root range includes arising and growth, but Form IV with divine subject and object suffix selects caused origination.

topics.headline: genesis language colors the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices origination as a genesis-like bringing forth into a new state, while the local verb remains a finite causative action.
topics.reason: Derivative noun fields support genesis and emergent-state pressure, but local morphology keeps the word as a causative verb.

topics.headline: subjunctive projection differs from completed creation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this origination as capacity-projection rather than a completed creation report.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as imperfect subjunctive under the capacity construction, unlike same-surah perfect creation reports.

topics.headline: unknown re-origination prepares remembered origination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this verb as a hinge from unknown re-origination in 56:61 to remembered first origination in 56:62.
topics.reason: Same-surah recurrence and the following knowledge verb support the bridge, while local syntax still makes the present word the second verb of the capacity clause.

topics.headline: the second act escalates the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from altered likeness-patterns into direct re-origination, with the second verb carrying the stronger personal pressure.
topics.reason: The second verb follows the first in coordination and includes the addressees as its attached direct object; its hamza also audibly marks the break into origination.

topics.headline: surah-local recurrence reinforces the creation thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the direct object of re-origination is the same death-addressed audience, within a wider origination thread in 56:35, 56:61, 56:62, and 56:72.
topics.reason: The recurrence supports a surah-level pattern and pronoun continuity, but does not replace the local Form IV subjunctive parse.

words.prose: {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) attaches the final unknown expression to the re-origination verb. It governs {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), and the whole phrase {{ar:مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:mā lā taʿlamūna}}) becomes the domain or mode in which re-origination occurs. The containment image remains useful: the unknown is not just an adjective added to re-creation, but the field into which the addressees are originated. Because the phrase comes after {{ar:نُنْشِئَكُمْ}} ({{tr:nunshiʾakum}}), the line first fixes who is re-originated and only then discloses that the mode is beyond their knowledge.

topics.headline: the unknown phrase is the re-origination domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah says re-origination happens within what they do not know, not simply that re-origination is unfamiliar.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the relative pronoun the complement of the preposition, with the phrase attached to the re-origination verb.

topics.headline: containment image becomes modal domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the unknown pictured as a containing field, while the abstract context allows domain or mode rather than literal place alone.
topics.reason: The preposition supports containment and circumstance, but the complement is an abstract relative clause of non-knowledge.

topics.headline: the unknown arrives after the object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sequence fixing the addressed object first, then withholding the mode until the final phrase.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase follows the verb with its attached object suffix.

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) gives {{ar:فِي}} ({{tr:fī}}) a content-bearing complement, but it does not name that content by itself. As a relative pronoun, it receives its identity from {{ar:لَا تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:lā taʿlamūna}}), so the domain of re-origination is defined precisely as what the addressees do not know. This keeps the new mode open-ended: not a named place, body, or manner, and not a negating particle here. With this word, the ayah's final movement shifts from divine action to unresolved specification.

topics.headline: the following clause defines the pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the unknown domain is grammatically created by the following non-knowledge clause.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as a relative pronoun governed by the preposition and linked to the following clause.

topics.headline: relative breadth withholds a named form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse generalizes the mode as whatever they do not know, instead of naming the new form directly.
topics.reason: The surface can serve other functions elsewhere, but local grammar selects the relative pronoun rather than negation or an independent indefinite noun.

topics.headline: the final phrase shifts into unresolved specification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's landing begin to move away from what God does and toward what the addressees cannot specify.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun begins the phrase that carries the ayah into its final negated knowledge verb.

words.gloss_range: simple negation particle scoped over the final knowledge verb inside the relative clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the knowledge verb negated by this particle

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) negates {{ar:تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿlamūna}}) inside the relative clause. The following verb is not jussive, so the particle reports non-knowledge rather than prohibiting knowledge. Its scope stays inside {{ar:مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:mā lā taʿlamūna}}): divine replacement and re-origination remain asserted, while the addressees' knowledge of the mode is denied. As the penultimate word, the long open vowel slows the line into an epistemic closure rather than a positive description.

topics.headline: the particle reports non-knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah states a limit of knowledge, not a command not to know.
topics.reason: The negated verb is an imperfect indicative form, so the particle functions as verbal negation rather than prohibition or categorical nominal negation.

topics.headline: negation is local to the knowledge verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the negation creates an epistemic boundary while leaving divine action fully intact.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence places the negated verb inside the relative expression governed by the preceding preposition.

topics.headline: negation prepares the final landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final landing prepared as negated knowledge rather than named re-creation mechanics.
topics.reason: The particle immediately precedes the final word and its long vowel leads into the closing knowledge verb.

words.gloss_range: second-person plural imperfect knowledge verb negated inside the relative clause; broad cognitive apprehension rather than recognition of a named item

words.prose: {{ar:تَعْلَمُونَ}} ({{tr:taʿlamūna}}) closes the ayah by making the barrier cognitive. Under {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), the imperfect describes ongoing non-knowledge, but not a command and not a claim that the divine act is negated. The object remains the relative {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), so what is withheld is the mode or domain of re-origination, not a named thing the addressees fail to recognize. The second-person plural ending assigns that limit to the addressed group as a group, and Form I measures their own apprehension rather than whether someone has taught or informed them. The root field can evoke signs and knowable worlds, but locally it marks a domain without accessible markers; this final non-knowledge then turns forward to the next ayah's remembered knowledge (56:62) and participates in a broader non-knowledge formula (2:232, 16:74, 24:19). Its closing sound also returns the ayah's opening capacity edge and threads the earlier addressee endings, carrying the line from power to unknowability without equating the roots.

topics.headline: the final verb states ongoing non-knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing as a descriptive limit on present human knowing, not a one-time past ignorance or prohibition.
topics.reason: The imperfect indicative under simple negation supports ongoing descriptive non-knowledge; the stronger claim of inherent absolute ignorance is kept as pressure rather than overstated.

topics.headline: the unknown object remains grammatically concrete
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ignorance is grammatically anchored to the relative object while the exact new form remains unnamed.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun supplies the object of the transitive knowledge verb, while the lexical range supports broad cognitive apprehension.

topics.headline: knowledge-root imagery makes the domain signless
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the unknown mode as a domain without accessible markers, while the local clause stops short of naming it as an actual new world.
topics.reason: The root-family evidence supports sign and domain associations, but local syntax only asserts non-knowledge of the re-origination domain.

topics.headline: the knowledge limit is addressed to the group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing limit belongs to the addressed plural group and measures their own apprehension, not whether someone has taught them.
topics.reason: The verb is Form I second-person plural, with the subject agreement tied to the direct addressees.

topics.headline: non-knowledge links to origination and formulaic boundaries
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final non-knowledge as both locally bound to re-origination and resonant with recurring epistemic-boundary wording (2:232, 16:74, 24:19).
topics.reason: The recurring formula and root-pair evidence support an epistemic-boundary pattern, but here it is specialized to the unknown mode of re-origination.

topics.headline: the ayah lands on ignorance before remembered knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ending on negated knowledge, which the next ayah reverses into remembered knowledge in 56:62.
topics.reason: The word is final in 56:61 and same-root knowledge language appears in the next ayah as an affirmed appeal.

topics.headline: sound returns from opening capacity to closing knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah framed by related onset sounds and repeated addressee endings, moving from capacity to unknowability without equating the roots.
topics.reason: The opening preposition and final verb share an onset pattern, and the addressed suffix sounds recur across the object words.

topics.headline: scope, echo, and bridge converge at the last word
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final word doing more than naming knowledge: it closes the current unknown, ties to the origination field, and prepares 56:62.
topics.reason: The final verb is locally negated, adjacent to the origination field, and echoed by the next ayah's affirmed knowledge language.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The addressed object remains كُمْ across نبدل أمثالكم and ننشئكم, while في ما لا تعلمون withholds the resulting mode.
baseline_models.mechanism: Changing an image without necessarily replacing its substance, followed by fresh origination, permits continuity of the addressed identity through discontinuity of its present embodiment.

activation_trace.role: Change of a thing's image while its substance remains makes the first verb a transformation of embodiment.
The pictured exemplar supplies the form or representation that can be changed.
Fresh bringing-into-being supplies the second operation after alteration of form.
Negated cognitive disclosure keeps the new condition genuinely unspecified.

changed_reading.before: One present body is simply removed and another is supplied.
changed_reading.after: The present likeness can be reconfigured while the same addressed 'you' is freshly brought into an unknown mode.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: نبدل أمثالكم combines substitution with the plural 'your counterparts,' then distinguishes that act from ننشئكم.
baseline_models.mechanism: One person or group can be displaced by analogous successors, while the conjunction opens a second horizon in which the displaced addressees themselves are originated anew.

activation_trace.role: One thing taking another's place supplies literal succession.
Similarity and counterpart status define the successors as analogues rather than identical returns.
Fresh creation prevents collective replacement from exhausting the promise made to 'you.'

changed_reading.before: The verse speaks only of each individual's later recreation.
changed_reading.after: It can hold collective succession by counterparts and the addressees' own later origination together without collapsing them.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ننشئكم can carry growth and elevation as well as initial creation, and it is followed by في ما.
baseline_models.mechanism: Origination may be staged maturation or rising into a condition, so the unknown concerns an unfolding order rather than only an instantaneous manufacture.

activation_trace.role: The growth and upbringing of the young supplies a developmental trajectory.
Rising and elevation give that trajectory a movement into another level or condition.
The withheld knowledge leaves the stages and destination outside present experience.

changed_reading.before: ننشئكم denotes a single completed act of recreation.
changed_reading.after: It may denote being raised or grown into an unknown condition whose process is as undisclosed as its result.

context_deltas.mechanism: Measured creation, form-bearing reproductive material, and apportioned death turn 'likenesses' into reproducible configurations: a present instantiation can end without exhausting the agency that measured it.

activation_trace.role: The represented form is the focus-ayah anchor for a configuration that can be instantiated again.
Fresh origination realizes the measured configuration beyond its current instance.
Measuring and proportioning creation supplies a reproducible ordering operation.
Reproductive material from which form is measured supplies an observed small-origin-to-shaped-being transition.
Deliberate apportioning makes death part of the same ordered agency rather than a failure of creation.

structural_cues: The sequence moves from reproductive material (56:58), through disputed creative agency (56:59), to apportioned death (56:60) and then replacement plus origination (56:61).
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies measured creation, form-bearing reproductive material, and planned death; I infer that the same measuring agency can instantiate the addressed identity beyond death. context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an unknown future setting and a known first origination; I infer that ignorance attaches to modality, not to agency or possibility. Alternatively, 56:62 may offer only a general proof and leave every detail of 56:61 open.

context_deltas.mechanism: Tilling supplies prepared material, but growth belongs to another agency and the same crop can instead be rendered fragments; this makes origination a directed developmental process whose outcome is not controlled by its visible preparers.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same pronominally continuous water can be rendered bitter without ceasing to be the referenced water; this gives a concrete local analogue for continuity of 'you' through replacement of a present likeness.

changed_reading.before: لا تعلمون means only that factual information is missing.
changed_reading.after: It may also suggest an order not indexed by familiar marks of identity, requiring orientation by the named creator rather than projection from present signs.

strongest_changes: The first-origination echo in 56:62 confines ignorance chiefly to future mode rather than creative possibility.
Measured generation and the water counterfactual support continuity of the addressed identity through discontinuity of present form.
Crop growth and latent fire turn origination from static replacement into directed emergence from an unpromising or unlike source.
Crushing, attached loss, and deprivation keep the unspecified future condition valence-open.
summary.what_was_special: The tightest activation came from the water and fire sequences: water retains reference across radical property-change, while fire emerges from a created tree and is explicitly made a reminder. Together they separate continuity of 'you' from continuity of the present likeness without pretending to describe the unknown result.
remaining_uncertainties: أمثالكم may designate successor persons, embodied forms, or likeness-patterns; the focus construction does not force one.
في ما may leave an unknown state, domain, process, or created configuration unspecified.
The agricultural, water, and fire passages may prove agency without mapping the mechanism of human origination.
The developmental and sign-system activations depend on form-distant branches and should remain exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Replacement by counterparts and origination beyond present knowledge.** `ب د ل` **B001** supplies substitution; `م ث ل` **B001** likeness and counterpart; `ن ش ء` **B006** bringing into being; `ع ل م` **B001** knowing as clear. The two verbs distinguish exchanging present forms from initiating in an unknown domain. **Abductive move:** I infer that measured death clears a position for transformation and re-origination. **Reading change:** resurrection is framed as controlled continuity-through-difference.

2. **Transformation follows a model without being mere duplication.** `ب د ل` **B002** supplies alteration or transformation and `م ث ل` **B010** compliance with a model. **Abductive move:** I infer that `أمثالكم` preserves pattern while `ننشئكم` permits a mode not presently known. **Reading change:** likeness becomes a rule of continuity, not proof of identical material form.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The protected but descending recitation at 56:77–80 gave another model of continuity across domains: preserved identity can enter a new accessible placement.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Unoutstripped power includes both succession and unfamiliar re-formation.** `ب د ل` (B001, one thing taking another’s place) operates on `م ث ل` (B001, likeness or comparable form), then `ن ش ء` (B006, bringing into being with formation) acts on the hearers within what `ع ل م` (B001, knowing as a thing becomes clear) is negated from them. Ayat 56–60 move from recompense to measured death; ayat 62–66 answer ignorance with first origin and then model contingent crop loss. The packet supplies replacement and origination as coordinated but distinct acts; I infer a range wider than reassembling an identical body. Unknown form limits the audience’s forecast, not the stated agency.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 56:88–94 discloses relational outcomes—brought-near relief, right-hand peace, and punitive exposure—confirming that unknown re-formation opens into differentiated destiny rather than mere replacement in place.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu anlam sıradan benzerlikten ayrılır; cezalandırılan kişinin uğradığı işlem başkalarını caydıran görünür bir sonuç doğurur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, cezalandırma adlarını ve belirli tümleçlerle kurulan cezalandırma, yaralama ve karşılık verme yapılarını içerir; yapıya bağlı ayrıntılar yalın kök anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimseye ağır, yaralayıcı veya karşılık niteliğinde bir ceza uygulayıp onu başkalarının sakınacağı ibret verici bir duruma getirmektir.

facets.statement: Cezalandırılan kişiye yapılan ağır işlem, yalnız ona karşı bir yaptırım değil, başkalarını da caydıran ibret verici bir sonuçtur.
Özel yapılarda eylem, öldürülen kişinin bedenini kesip bozmayı, karşılık olarak öldürmeyi veya birinden öç alır gibi hakkını almayı anlatabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ağır cezalandırma ile başkalarını caydıracak ibret oluşturma bağını ortaklaştırır; bazı biçimler bedenin kesilip bozulmasına, karşılık olarak öldürmeye ve hakkın karşılığını almaya özelleşir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Ağır işlemin hem cezalandırılan kişiye yöneldiğini hem de başkalarını caydıran bir örnek sonuç doğurduğunu birlikte anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Ağır yaptırım, ibret oluşturma ve caydırma sonuçlarının tümünü korur.

contextual_glosses.text: onu ibret olsun diye ağır biçimde cezalandırdı
contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişiye uygulanan yaptırımın başkalarını da sakındırması amaçlandığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yaptırımın hedefini, ağırlığını ve başkalarına dönük caydırıcı sonucunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yetkili birinin suçun karşılığını uyguladığı veya bir kişinin hakkının karşılığını aldığı özel yapılarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Karşılık verme ve cezalandırma yönlerini birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal cezalandırılanı görünür bir ibret durumuna getiren ağır işlemi ve bazı özel karşılık türlerini kapsar; komşu dalın odağı ise cezayla tekrarın önlenmesi ve başkalarının korkutulmasıdır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, başka bir durumla benzerliği üzerinden aktarılan kalıplaşmış veya örnek niteliğindeki sözü, böyle bir sözü söylemeyi ve bir şiir dizesini bu amaçla anmayı birlikte doğrular. Dal çerçevesi bu sözlü kullanım alanını doğru ayırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal iki şeyin yalnızca benzemesini değil, bir durumu başka bir durum üzerinden anlatmak için söylenen ve dolaşım kazanan sözü kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, özlü örnek sözün adını ve onu söyleme ya da bir dizeyle örneklendirme yapılarını ayırır; eylem kalıpları yalın adın bütün kullanımlarına taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir durumdaki anlamı benzer başka bir duruma taşıyan, örnek olarak söylenen ve çoğu kez dilden dile dolaşan özlü sözdür; böyle bir sözü veya şiir dizesini örnek diye anma eylemini de kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir şey hakkında söylenen söz, benzer bir başka durumu açıklamak için örnek söz olarak aktarılır ve kalıplaşarak dolaşıma girebilir.
Konuşan, bir örnek sözü söyleyebilir veya bir şiir dizesini aynı işlevle anarak kendi durumuna dayanak yapabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, benzer iki durum arasında anlam taşıyan ve örnek olarak söylenen söz çekirdeğinde birleşir; dolaşımda olan özlü söz, böyle bir söz söyleme ve bir dizeyi örnek gösterme kullanımları bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir durumun anlamını benzer başka bir durum üzerinden açıklayan özlü sözün kendisini ve onu örnek diye anma kullanımını kapsar.

error_profile.preserves: Söz olma, benzer durumlar arasında anlam taşıma ve örnek gösterilme özelliklerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bilinen ve sıkça tekrarlanan kalıplaşmış örnek sözlerden bahsedilen bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Henüz yaygınlaşmamış örnek sözleri ve bir dizeyi örnek diye anma eylemini dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şiir dizesinin mevcut durumu açıklamak veya desteklemek için anıldığı bağlamda kullanılır.

Daha dar bir yorum, gecenin uyku sonrasında kalan bölümünü veya o sırada gerçekleşen kalkışı belirtir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi bilmek, tanımak ve onu gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavramak; böylece bilgisizlikten çıkmaktır. Haber verilmesi, öğretme, öğrenme ve bilgi bakımından üstün gelme bu çekirdekten hareket eden, belirli biçimlere bağlı kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi bilme, tanıma ve gerçeğine uygun biçimde kavrama durumu bilgisizliğin karşıtıdır.

Bildirme, öğretme ve öğrenme biçimleri bilginin bir başkasına ulaştırılması ya da kişinin onu edinmesi süreçlerini anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi başkasından ayıran belirgin izi dalın ortak çekirdeği olarak açıkça destekler. Bayrak, belirgin dağ, yol belirtisi, kumaş deseni ve savaş işareti gibi örnekler bu çekirdeğin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir; tanınmış kişi ve son zaman belirtisi ise benzetme veya gösterme ilişkisine bağlı uzantılardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Ayırt edici iz çıplak çekirdektir; savaşçı, kumaş, sarık ve belirli zaman göstergesiyle kurulan anlamlar kendi kuruluşlarına bağlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başkalarından ayıran, tanınmasını sağlayan veya ona götüren belirgin iz ya da işarettir. Bayrak, uzaktan seçilen dağ, yol belirtisi, kumaş kenarı ve sonradan konan tanıtıcı izler bu işlevin farklı gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi veya kişiyi başkalarından ayırıp tanınır kılan belirgin iz ya da işaret çekirdeği oluşturur.
Bayrak, belirgin dağ, yol belirtisi ve kumaşın kenar deseni yön bulduran veya tanıtan somut gerçekleşmelerdir.
Savaşçının, kumaşın veya sarığın ayırt edici bir işaretle donatılması belirli kuruluşlara bağlı eylemsel kullanımdır.
Tanınmış bir kişinin belirgin bir bayrağa benzetilmesi ve yaklaşan son zamanı gösteren belirti, işaret çekirdeğinin uzantılarıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ayırt edici izi ortak temel sayar ve bayrak, yüksek ya da belirgin dağ, yol göstergesi, kumaş kenarı, kına ve sonradan yerleştirilen tanıtıcı işaretleri bu temelde toplar. Tanınmış kişi ile yaklaşan son zamanın belirtisi de görünürlük ve gösterme işlevinden doğan uzantılardır.

concept_map.definition: İnsanın üst dudağında veya devenin üst dudak bölgesinde bulunan belirgin yarıktır. Aynı dal, bu özelliği taşıyanı niteleyen biçimi ve üst dudağı yarma eylemini de kapsar.

facets.statement: Üst dudakta bulunan yarık, dalın anatomik çekirdeğini oluşturur.
Üst dudağı yarık insan veya üst dudak bölgesinde bu belirti bulunan deve, özelliği taşıyan varlık olarak nitelenir.
Birinin üst dudağını yarmak, anatomik sonucun oluşturulmasını bildiren eylemsel kullanımdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yarığın yerini üst dudak olarak ortak biçimde sınırlar ve yarıklı insanı bu özellikle niteler. Toplu tanıklık, devenin üst dudak bölgesindeki karşılığını ve üst dudağı yarma eylemini de aynı dalda gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: İnsan veya devenin üst dudak bölgesindeki belirgin yarığı adlandıran temel kullanım için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yarığın türünü ve özellikle üst dudaktaki yerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir insanı veya deveyi üst dudak bölgesindeki yarıkla niteleyen bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Özelliğin taşıyıcıda bulunmasını ve anatomik yerini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin üst dudağında yarık oluşturma eylemini anlatan kuruluşta kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Eylemi, etkilenen kişiyi ve üst dudak sınırını korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tek bir su birikimi türü tanımlamaz; aynı sözlük biçimi için deniz ve suyu bol kuyu olmak üzere iki ayrı karşılık verir. Dal korunabilir, ancak geçici çerçevedeki ortak su kütlesi görüntüsü yerine bu açık seçeneklilik tanıma yazılmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Deniz ile suyu bol kuyu tek bir ara nesnede birleştirilmez; bunlar aynı biçimin kaynaklarda verilen iki ayrı sözlük karşılığıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak sözlük biçiminin deniz ve suyu bol kuyu karşılıklarını ayrı ayrı korur; bunlardan genel bir su birikintisi anlamı türetmez.

concept_map.definition: Aynı sözlük biçiminin bir kullanımda denizi, başka bir kullanımda ise suyu bol kuyuyu adlandırmasıdır. İki karşılık, genel bir su birikintisi anlamında kaynaştırılmaz.

facets.statement: Dal, aynı adın iki ayrı su varlığına verilen sözlük karşılıklarını birlikte kaydeder.
Bir kaynak karşılığında ad, geniş tuzlu su kütlesi olan denizi gösterir.
Diğer ve daha yaygın kaynak karşılığında ad, suyu çok olan kuyuyu gösterir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu tanıklık iki karşılığı yan yana verir: bir aktarım sözcüğü deniz olarak açıklar, öteki tanıklıklar ise suyu bol kuyu anlamını destekler. Kaynaklara özgü ayrı claim kimlikleri bulunmadığı için bu karşıtlık ortak özet içinde, atıf uydurulmadan korunur.

concept_gloss.text: deniz ya da suyu bol kuyu
concept_gloss.applicability: Sözlük biçiminin kaynaklarda verilen iki ayrı karşılığını eksiltmeden birlikte göstermek gerektiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Deniz ve suyu bol kuyu karşılıklarını birbirine indirgemeden korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sözlük biçiminin geniş su kütlesi karşılığıyla kullanıldığı tanıklığa özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Deniz karşılığını doğal ve doğrudan biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Aynı biçim için tanıklanan suyu bol kuyu karşılığını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sözlük biçiminin bol su içeren kuyu karşılığıyla kullanıldığı tanıklıklara özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Kuyu türünü ve suyunun çokluğu koşulunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Aynı biçim için tanıklanan deniz karşılığını dışarıda bırakır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal aynı sözlük biçiminin suyu bol kuyu karşılığını da bağımsız bir seçenek olarak taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal deniz yanında büyük ırmak ve farklı büyüklükte su alanlarına uzanan genel bir geniş su kapsamına sahiptir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Odak dalın deniz karşılığı, komşu dalın geniş ve çok su çekirdeğiyle örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Örtüşme yalnızca deniz karşılığındadır; odak dalın kuyu seçeneği komşuda bulunmaz, komşunun büyük ırmak ve genel su genişliği ise odak dalın tanımına girmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kuyunun kendisini suyunun bol olması koşuluyla adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kuyudaki kovadan dökülen veya havuza taşan suyu, kokusunu ve taşma olayını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: suyu bol kuyu ile kuyu suyu
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal kuyu çevresinde suyun çokluğu ve görünür birikimiyle ilişkilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal suyu taşıyan kuyuyu niteler; komşu dal ise kuyudan dökülen suyu ve taşma sürecini merkez alır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi temel adı doğan veya atmaca türünden yırtıcı kuş için verir ve geçici dal görüntüsünü doğrular. Çevik ve zeki erkek nitelemesi ise kuş adından türetilmiş ayrı bir biçimdir; kuşun tanımına doğrudan katılmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek yırtıcı kuş adıdır; çevik ve zeki erkek nitelemesi yalnızca bu addan türeyen biçime bağlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak dal doğan veya atmaca türünden kuş adını tanımlar; insan nitelemesi türemiş bir sözcüksel uzantı olarak bağımlı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Doğan veya atmaca türünden bir yırtıcı kuş adıdır. Bu kuş adından türetilen bir niteleme, çevik ve zeki bir erkeği anlatır.

facets.statement: Ad, doğan veya atmaca türünden avcı bir kuşu gösterir.
Kuş adından türeyen insan nitelemesi, çevik ve zeki bir erkeği belirtir.

error_profile.preserves: Yırtıcı kuş sınıfını ve doğan ile atmaca karşılıklarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kuş adından türemiş insan nitelemesinin kullanıldığı bağlama özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: İnsan oluşu ile çeviklik ve zekâ niteliklerini birlikte korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal doğan veya atmaca türünü genel bir adla karşılar ve bu addan insan nitelemesi türetir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal özellikle zeki ve keskin bakışlı doğanlara verilen bir adı belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: doğan adı ile zeki doğan nitelemesi
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal doğan türünden yırtıcı kuşları adlandırır ve zekâ çağrışımını paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalda zekâ kuştan türetilen insan niteliğinde belirginleşir; komşuda ise doğrudan belirli doğanların özelliğidir.
